@@ -14,14 +14,7 @@ The following <%= params.size %> parameters are defined in this manual:
 
 <%- params.each do |param| -%>
 | <%= param.name %>
-<%-   if param.schema_known? -%>
 | <%= param.schema.to_pretty_s %>
-<%-   else -%>
-<%-     param.schemas.each do |cond_schema| -%>
-<%-       next unless cond_schema.cond.could_be_satisfied_by_cfg_arch?(cfg_arch) -%>
-a| <%= cond_schema.schema.to_pretty_s %> when <%= cond_schema.cond.to_asciidoc %>

-<%-   end -%>
 a| <%= param.defined_by_condition.to_asciidoc -%>
 a| <%= param.description %>
body: This template now always prints `param.schema.to_pretty_s` for the parameter type/range. Since many parameter schemas were broadened to the RV64 superset and the RV32-specific limits moved into `requirements`, the generated manual will no longer show architecture-specific valid ranges unless requirements are also rendered. Consider adding a column/row that includes `param.requirements_condition` (e.g., as AsciiDoc) so readers can see the RV32 constraints.

body:
The parameter table no longer shows conditional schemas, but it also doesn’t display `param.requirements_condition`. For parameters where RV32-specific limits were moved from schema into requirements (e.g., max values depending on MXLEN), the “Valid Values” row will be misleading. Consider adding a “Requirements” row (or appending requirements text to “Valid Values”) so the manual still communicates configuration-dependent constraints.
```suggestion
| <%= param.schema.to_pretty_s %>
<% if param.respond_to?(:requirements_condition) && !param.requirements_condition.nil? && !param.requirements_condition.to_s.empty? -%>
h| Requirements
| <%= param.requirements_condition.respond_to?(:to_asciidoc) ? param.requirements_condition.to_asciidoc : param.requirements_condition.to_s %>
<% end -%>
```

diff_hunk:
@@ -77,7 +77,9 @@ def self.constrain_int(solver, term, schema_hsh)
       end
 
       if schema_hsh.key?("allOf")
-        constrain_int(solver, term, schema_hsh.fetch("allOf"))
+        schema_hsh.fetch("allOf").each do |h|
+          constrain_int(solver, term, h)
+        end
       end
body: Now that `allOf` is iterated, subschemas containing `$ref: .../uint32` / `.../uint64` will start applying the `$ref` constraints in `constrain_int`. Those constraints currently enforce a power-of-two shape (`term & (term-1) == 0`), which doesn't match `schema_defs.json#/$defs/uint32|uint64` (they are plain integer ranges). This can over-constrain parameters (e.g., IDs) and make Z3 results incorrect; consider implementing `$ref` by applying the referenced schema’s min/max (or resolving the ref) and reserving power-of-two logic for the dedicated `*pow2` defs instead.

       end
 
       if schema_hsh.key?("allOf")
-        constrain_int(solver, term, schema_hsh.fetch("allOf"))
+        schema_hsh.fetch("allOf").each do |h|
+          constrain_int(solver, term, h)
+        end
       end
body: `constrain_int` now correctly iterates `allOf`, but `constrain_bool` still calls itself with `schema_hsh.fetch("allOf")` (an Array) rather than iterating like the integer path. That means boolean constraints inside `allOf` will still be silently ignored; consider updating the boolean implementation to `each` over the `allOf` array too.
